must_include_papers.citation: Asgari et al., 2026. MorphBPE: Morphology-Aware Tokenization for Efficient LLM Training. Findings of ACL 2026.
must_include_papers.morphology_type: concatenative and non-concatenative; morphologically rich languages emphasized
must_include_papers.amount_type_morphological_supervision: Morpheme boundaries required for the training corpus during MorphBPE merge training; source of boundaries per language UNKNOWN from abstract/method sketch beyond 'available morphological annotations'. Inference needs no morphology.
must_include_papers.how_morphology_affects_tokenization: During tokenizer training, merge candidates that would cross morpheme boundaries are disallowed; frequency ranking otherwise unchanged.
must_include_papers.fallback_mechanism: Standard BPE behavior at inference; no special morphology runtime. UNKNOWN residual character policy beyond standard BPE.
must_include_papers.vocabulary_size: Matched across conditions; exact size UNKNOWN from abstract (controlled identical sizes in experiments).
must_include_papers.lm_evaluation: Decoder-only LMs 300M and 1B trained from scratch; reports reduced cross-entropy vs BPE under matched vocab/settings.
must_include_papers.downstream_evaluation: Belebele; significant gains for Russian and Arabic.
must_include_papers.morphology_evaluation: Intrinsic Morph Consistency F1 and Morph Edit Distance.
must_include_papers.main_result: MorphBPE improves morphological coherence and LM cross-entropy without materially shorter tokens; downstream gains on morphologically rich languages.
must_include_papers.limitations: Requires morpheme boundaries for full training corpus (not available for Chichewa at scale). BPE-centric (our strongest Chichewa LM baseline is Unigram). No Chichewa/Bantu evaluation. Gold-boundary quality and annotation cost UNKNOWN for low-resource settings.
must_include_papers.applicability_to_chichewa: MEDIUM for idea transfer (constrained merges); LOW for direct reuse without a corpus-scale morphological analyzer or large labeled set.
overlap_with_candidate_designs: 1_presegmentation_plus_subword (related but MorphBPE integrates constraint into BPE training rather than pure pre-tokenization)

must_include_papers.how_morphology_affects_tokenization: Morphologically-guided tokenization improves morphological alignment vs compression-only goals.

languages: Ge'ez script languages (four with morpheme annotation; vocab for two)

must_include_papers.supervised_unsupervised_weak: supervised morphological analysis integrated into vocabulary construction
must_include_papers.amount_type_morphological_supervision: Manually annotated morpheme data for four languages; morpheme-aware vocabulary released for two.

must_include_papers.citation: Saleva & Lignos, 2021. The Effectiveness of Morphology-aware Segmentation in Low-Resource Neural Machine Translation. EACL SRW 2021.
must_include_papers.supervised_unsupervised_weak: morphologically-based segmentations from LMVR and MORSEL vs BPE
must_include_papers.amount_type_morphological_supervision: Method-dependent (LMVR/MORSEL); not a large manual gold morph corpus described as primary; treat as morphology-aware algorithms rather than full analyzers—details of training supervision: UNKNOWN beyond method names.
must_include_papers.base_tokenizer: BPE (token/sentence level) vs LMVR vs MORSEL
must_include_papers.how_morphology_affects_tokenization: Morphology-aware segmenters replace or compare against BPE segmentation for NMT inputs.
must_include_papers.morphology_affects_vocabulary_learning: UNKNOWN (segmentation methods produce units used as NMT vocabulary/input)

must_include_papers.citation: Richburg et al., 2020. An Evaluation of Subword Segmentation Strategies for Neural Machine Translation of Morphologically Rich Languages. WiNLP 2020.

languages: multiple NMT corpora (paper experiments; language list details treated as multi-corpus)
must_include_papers.morphology_type: general; motivated by open vocabulary and segmentation ambiguity
must_include_papers.supervised_unsupervised_weak: unsupervised Unigram LM segmentation + probabilistic regularization
must_include_papers.base_tokenizer: Unigram language model subword segmentation (SentencePiece lineage)
must_include_papers.how_morphology_affects_tokenization: No explicit morphology; probabilistic multi-segmentation training.
must_include_papers.morphology_affects_inference_segmentatio: Optional sampling at train; deterministic MAP segmentation typically at inference (common practice; exact inference default: UNKNOWN if paper-specific).
must_include_papers.fallback_mechanism: Character-level units in Unigram vocabulary construction (standard).

must_include_papers.citation: Mager et al., 2022. BPE vs. Morphological Segmentation: A Case Study on Machine Translation of Four Polysynthetic Languages. Findings of ACL 2022.
must_include_papers.supervised_unsupervised_weak: supervised and unsupervised morphological segmentation vs BPE
must_include_papers.amount_type_morphological_supervision: Supervised morph methods use labeled morph data; unsupervised morph algorithms also evaluated; new morph datasets contributed for two languages.
must_include_papers.how_morphology_affects_tokenization: Morph segmentations used as MT input units vs BPE.
must_include_papers.morphology_evaluation: Segmentation scores; supervised better at segmentation, worse at MT.

must_include_papers.applicability_to_chichewa: MEDIUM: unsupervised morph can beat BPE; supervised morph gold may not help LM/MT.
overlap_with_candidate_designs: supports unsupervised over heavy supervised morph
must_include_papers.notes: Supports using unsupervised signals rather than memorizing small gold sets.

candidate_family_novelty.name: pre_segmentation_plus_Unigram_fallback
candidate_family_novelty.novelty_risk_rationale: Classic pipeline: morphological pre-segmentation then statistical subword (Morfessor-style / MoVoC hybrid / Otani-style). MorphBPE related work explicitly discusses pre-tokenization morph + subword. Saleva & Lignos and Mager et al. extensively study this family for MT.

candidate_family_novelty.name: boundary_biased_Unigram
candidate_family_novelty.novelty_risk_rationale: Unigram itself is Kudo 2018 / Bostrom-Durrett 2020 / Richburg 2020. Explicit boundary bias inside Unigram training (soft or hard constraints without full morph analyzer) is less standardized than MorphBPE's hard BPE constraint, but still close in spirit to morphology-constrained training.

candidate_family_novelty.name: morphology_constrained_BPE
candidate_family_novelty.novelty_risk_rationale: Directly overlaps MorphBPE (Asgari et al. 2026): disallow merges crossing morpheme boundaries during BPE training; inference standard BPE. 'First for Chichewa' is not sufficient novelty.

candidate_family_novelty.name: hybrid_affix_stem_vocabulary
candidate_family_novelty.novelty_risk_rationale: MoVoC integrates supervised morpheme units into vocab with BPE. Hybrid affix/stem lexica are long-standing in morphologically motivated tokenizers and analyzers.

candidate_family_novelty.name: statistical_affix_plus_character_fallback
candidate_family_novelty.novelty_risk_rationale: Unsupervised affix/stem induction (Morfessor lineage, Mager unsupervised morph) + character residual is a known toolkit pattern; less packaged as a modern 8k Unigram competitor under fixed LM budgets for Bantu.

candidate_family_novelty.name: whole_word_memorization_regularization
candidate_family_novelty.novelty_risk_rationale: Vocabulary allocation / whole-word retention is a common engineering lever in multilingual tokenization; not morphology-specific novelty. Limited distinct morphology story for SC4.
strongest_overlap: general SentencePiece user practices; not a single dominant morph paper in must-include set

candidate_family_novelty.name: word_family_consistency_regularization
candidate_family_novelty.novelty_risk_rationale: MorphBPE Morph Consistency F1 formalizes related goals; Marco & Fraser (cited by MorphBPE) study consistency. Distinct algorithm may exist but concept is published.

candidate_family_novelty.name: stochastic_segmentation
candidate_family_novelty.novelty_risk_rationale: Kudo 2018 subword regularization is the canonical method. BPE-Dropout is related. Claiming novelty for stochastic segmentation alone is unsupported.

candidate_family_novelty.name: character_byte_fallback
candidate_family_novelty.novelty_risk_rationale: Standard in Unigram/BPE/character baselines; our character baseline already exists. Not a standalone novel method.
